title: Shifting the indegrees of an orientation
statement: Let $G$ be a finite $(m+n)$-regular simple graph, and suppose $n < m$. If $G$ is $(m,n)$-orientable — that is, its edges admit an orientation in which every vertex has indegree equal to $m$ or to $n$ — then $G$ is also $(m-1,\,n+1)$-orientable.
replaced:
\emph{Deduce that if \texttt{G} is \texttt{(m,n)}-orientable and \texttt{m > n},
then \texttt{G} is also \texttt{(m-1, n+1)}-orientable.}
